analysis.title: "Always Darkest Before The Dawn?" Hedge Funds Are The Most Bearish In Five Years While The S&P Sits 1% From A Record
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell less than 50bps last week and sits 1.1% below its high, but hedge fund portfolios took heavy losses. Goldman Prime Brokerage shows US long/short net leverage at 43.4%, the 0th percentile on a five-year lookback.

Fundamental L/S, Systematic and Multi-Strat funds each lost more than 1% on the same day last Thursday, the first time since COVID per Goldman's Peart. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest declines on record and is at its lowest since April 2025.

Goldman's Vol Panic Index rose 3 points last Wednesday and reached nearly 8 out of 10 by Friday, the first near-panic reading since late July. VVIX jumped 17 points, one of its largest one-day moves in four years.

The de-grossing was driven by long sales, not short pressing. Global equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week and single stocks for a 6th straight week, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1. US single stocks saw the largest de-grossing since late July.

Money rotated into defensives. US net buying in Staples was the largest since July 2025 (+1.8 standard deviations) and in Real Estate the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs). BofA warns defensive buying is a feature of bubble markets.

Asia-focused fundamental L/S managers are down 8.9% month to date and China-focused funds down 10.9%. The weighted YTD return for Asia managers is 14.5% but the median is 2.7%, meaning a few big winners carry the group.

The rebound off last week's lows reflects less selling, not new buying. Privorotsky says the demand side never changed, supply from financing and risk reduction is abating, and people have barely begun to re-risk.

CTAs remain long about $50bn of global equities, $36bn of it in the S&P. Goldman's model has them buying $114.4bn in a rally over the next month but selling $172.5bn in a decline. The S&P-specific read is roughly $15bn of upside buying versus roughly $60bn of selling in a 2SD selloff.
SPX pivot levels are 7717 short term, 7532 medium and 7070 long. With the S&P at 7,676 on Monday, the short-term trigger is about 0.5% away.

The bull case rests on supportive data. SK Hynix rose 10% overnight after sequential revenue growth of 32%, Celestica guided to $40bn of 2027 revenue, and about 27% of the index is in an open buyback window, rising to about 50% by the end of the week.

Wednesday's hyperscaler earnings are the near-term test. Buyside whispers are Azure growth around the high 40s% and Google Cloud around the mid 90s%. Privorotsky says Azure probably needs a guidance raise, and a capacity-driven miss could be even more bullish for the scarcity premium.

Credit is the bear-side focal point. Privorotsky says credit is still flashing yellow to red relative to equities. Goldman's Lynam expects spreads to widen 5-15bps by mid-December, with AI-related issuers facing heavy supply.

Global AI-related issuance is about $610bn this year, and hyperscalers are only about 38% of it. Goldman's earnings preview says Meta turned FCF-negative and flagged multi-year equity funding needs via new Class C shares, and its CDS spreads widened.
Goldman's Microsoft FY28 capex estimate is $319bn versus a Street consensus of $252bn. The market wants growth without another spending shock.

On the Fed, a hold is fully priced and Privorotsky sees two dissents as the central expectation. Hatzius expects a 25bp hike to 4-4.25% on December 9, while the market has priced four hikes, which Goldman thinks is too many.

Goldman's short-macro trader Bingham flags a front-end-led steepener if the AI drawdown worsens sharply as the most painful scenario for participants. The article's view is that a squeeze is possible but not an all-clear, and the index may be the last to adjust until credit confirms the bounce.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's FY28 capex estimate of $319bn is above the Street's $252bn. Azure needs a guidance raise to be properly supportive per the buyside whisper.
Goldman's preview says Meta turned FCF-negative, flagged multi-year equity funding needs via new Class C shares, and saw its CDS spreads widen.
Goldman's preview cites reports of idle NVDA racks that cannot switch on due to lack of power.
Buyside whisper for Google Cloud growth is around the mid 90s%, ahead of tonight's print.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds made their largest net purchases since July 2025, but BofA cautions defensive buying is a feature of bubble markets.
US net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs) as funds moved into bond-like sectors.
Funds made among the largest two-week institutional tech liquidations on record. Privorotsky favors being selective in the right pockets of tech and sees some demand returning in semis.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix reported (overnight, Oct 28 coverage): revenue +32% sequentially, operating profit +38%, margins 80%, and more than half of 2027/28 capacity already under long-term agreements. The stock rose 10%.
Celestica guided to $40bn of 2027 revenue, up 90% YoY. This is company guidance, not a reported figure.

Buyside whisper (not consensus, not reported) ahead of tonight's prints: Azure growth around the high 40s% and Google Cloud growth around the mid 90s%. Privorotsky says Azure probably needs a guidance raise.

Goldman earnings preview (pre-print): Meta turned FCF-negative and flagged multi-year equity funding needs via new Class C shares. Goldman's Microsoft FY28 capex estimate is $319bn versus a Street consensus of $252bn.
Amazon faces reports of idle NVDA racks that cannot switch on due to lack of power, per Goldman's earnings preview.

macro_indicators.reading: Hold fully priced, two dissents probably the central expectation
macro_indicators.interpretation: Zero dissents would be a dovish surprise. Three dissents would reinforce December as the next hike.
The market has priced four hikes, which Goldman thinks is too many. The article argues the Fed is hiking into the AI funding strain.
AI-related issuers face widening from heavy supply. Credit confirming or failing the equity bounce is the key signal.
The index looks calm while hedge fund positioning shows heavy damage underneath.

risk_factors: The AI buildout now needs outside money, and credit is pricing that in (spreads seen widening 5-15bps by mid-December).
Hyperscaler capex above Street expectations and Meta's negative FCF could produce a spending shock and lower multiples.
A Fed hike path (Goldman expects December 9) with four hikes priced by the market.
A front-end-led steepener if the AI drawdown worsens sharply (Bingham).
CTA selling of about $172.5bn in a down tape if equities fall.
Elevated energy prices, unresolved geopolitical risks and the midterm elections next week.
Defensive sector buying may signal bubble-type behavior, per BofA.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S net leverage 43.4%, 0th percentile on five years. US fundamental long/short ratio 1.503, 0th percentile.
Fundamental L/S net leverage 47.0%, a one-year low. Overall book net leverage 71.8%, 3rd percentile on one year.
Gross exposure fell, with the largest weekly de-grossing since July. Net exposure is still in the 0th percentile per Garrett's desk note.
Goldman Vol Panic Index near 8 out of 10, VVIX up 17 points in a day, GS Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025 and now below zero.
The correlation of the Risk Appetite gauge with the Nasdaq 100 (versus the equal-weight S&P) has risen steadily since 2024, so tech now dominates cross-asset moves.
CTA positioning: about $50bn long global equities, $36bn in the S&P. Model flows are +$114.4bn in an up tape and -$172.5bn in a down tape over the next month.
Privorotsky sees early signs of offense, with some buying in semis and some demand for upside vol, but says it is early.
Buyback window: about 27% of the index is open now, rising to about 50% by the end of the week.
geopolitical: Privorotsky says energy remains elevated and geopolitical risks are unresolved, and that the midterm elections next week are a source of known unknowns.
cross_bank_references: as BofA pointed out this morning, is not as safe as it sounds: defensive froth is a feature of bubble markets

tension_points.bull_case: Nets are at the lowest of the year, supply has abated, SK Hynix and Celestica data are strong, buybacks reopen, and Privorotsky says gross can start working again in the right pockets of tech. A strong Azure print could send the S&P to a record.
tension_points.bear_case: The funds sold because the AI buildout needs outside money, credit is flashing yellow to red, Goldman sees spreads widening 5-15bps by mid-December, and the Fed is expected to hike. The bounce is reduced selling, not new buying.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure failing to deliver a guidance raise tonight, or credit failing to confirm the bounce, with spreads widening 5-15bps toward mid-December.

tension_points.bull_case: A capacity-driven miss could be even more bullish for the scarcity premium, and demand for AI compute remains strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta is FCF-negative with CDS widening, Goldman's Microsoft FY28 capex estimate is $67bn above the Street, and spending may drive excess capacity, lower returns and lower multiples.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure needs a guidance raise to be properly supportive per the buyside whisper of growth around the high 40s%.
